findings.summary: The change adds a Today ordering rule (high-priority suggestions first), but the Today screen, the bounded-prompts criterion (which defines which five of six due goals become ordered cards) and the prompts requirements are not updated, so the ordering and truncation behavior is unspecified and untested.
findings.evidence: GoalPriorityField: "high-priority suggestions come first on Today"; RelationshipGoal: "Suggestions for high-priority goals are listed first on Today"; C.webapp.prompts.bounded: "Six due goals yield exactly five ordered cards" (unchanged); screen.today description unchanged

findings.summary: Priority-change coverage was added to the schedule-correctness criterion, but priority does not affect due dates or qualification under S.webapp.due and S.webapp.qualification, so the fixture claim tests the wrong concern while the ordering effect goes unverified.
findings.evidence: claim: "Fixed-clock fixtures cover zero logs, qualification, interval, depth and priority changes..."; S.webapp.due: "dueDate must equal anchor plus intervalDays" (no priority)

findings.summary: The new priority field is required on the entity, but no requirement defines its domain or default: S.webapp.qualification and GD.goals still list only interval and depth, and the 'default normal' rule appears only in the component description.
findings.evidence: entity field: "{ name: priority, type: \"enum high|normal\" }" (not optional); S.webapp.qualification: "an enabled goal must have intervalDays from 1 through 3650 and desiredDepth in light, meaningful or shared-time"; PriorityField: "default normal"
